verses.text: For the choirmaster. To the tune of “The Lilies of the Covenant.” A Psalm of Asaph. Hear us, O Shepherd of Israel, who leads Joseph like a flock; You who sit enthroned between the cherubim, shine forth

xrefs.text: From Zion, perfect in beauty, God shines forth.
And the city has no need of sun or moon to shine on it, because the glory of God illuminates the city, and the Lamb is its lamp.
You led Your people like a flock by the hand of Moses and Aaron.
The LORD reigns; let the nations tremble! He is enthroned above the cherubim; let the earth quake!
For “you were like sheep going astray,” but now you have returned to the Shepherd and Overseer of your souls.

verses.text: before Ephraim, Benjamin, and Manasseh. Rally Your mighty power and come to save us.

xrefs.text: Awake and rise to my defense, to my cause, my God and my Lord!
On the west side, the divisions of Ephraim are to camp under their standard: The leader of the Ephraimites is Elishama son of Ammihud,
Wake up, O Lord! Why are You sleeping? Arise! Do not reject us forever.
The LORD goes forth like a mighty one; He stirs up His zeal like a warrior. He shouts; yes, He roars in triumph over His enemies:
For the LORD is our Judge, the LORD is our lawgiver, the LORD is our King. It is He who will save us.

verses.text: Restore us, O God, and cause Your face to shine upon us, that we may be saved.

xrefs.text: Restore us to Yourself, O LORD, so we may return; renew our days as of old,
may the LORD cause His face to shine upon you and be gracious to you;
Restore us, O God of our salvation, and put away Your displeasure toward us.
Restore us, O God of Hosts, and cause Your face to shine upon us, that we may be saved.
Many ask, “Who can show us the good?” Shine the light of Your face upon us, O LORD.

verses.text: O LORD God of Hosts, how long will Your anger smolder against the prayers of Your people?

xrefs.text: Will You be angry with us forever? Will You draw out Your anger to all generations?

The LORD will never be willing to forgive him. Instead, His anger and jealousy will burn against that man, and every curse written in this book will fall upon him. The LORD will blot out his name from under heaven
And a Canaanite woman from that region came to Him, crying out, “Lord, Son of David, have mercy on me! My daughter is miserably possessed by a demon.
How long, O LORD? Will You be angry forever? Will Your jealousy burn like fire?
O LORD God of Hosts, the God of Israel, rouse Yourself to punish all the nations; show no mercy to the wicked traitors. Selah

verses.text: You fed them with the bread of tears and made them drink the full measure of their tears.

xrefs.text: My tears have been my food both day and night, while men ask me all day long, “Where is your God?”
The Lord will give you the bread of adversity and the water of affliction, but your Teacher will no longer hide Himself— with your own eyes you will see Him.
For I have eaten ashes like bread and mixed my drink with tears
Then He told me, “Son of man, I am going to cut off the supply of food in Jerusalem. They will anxiously eat bread rationed by weight, and in despair they will drink water by measure.
My soul refuses to touch them; they are loathsome food to me.

verses.text: You make us contend with our neighbors; our enemies mock us.

xrefs.text: We have become a reproach to our neighbors, a scorn and derision to those around us.
Was not Israel your object of ridicule? Was he ever found among thieves? For whenever you speak of him you shake your head.
Now, therefore, make a bargain with my master, the king of Assyria. I will give you two thousand horses— if you can put riders on them!
Whom have you taunted and blasphemed? Against whom have you raised your voice and lifted your eyes in pride? Against the Holy One of Israel!

But the Rabshakeh replied, “Has my master sent me to speak these words only to you and your master, and not to the men sitting on the wall, who are destined with you to eat their own dung and drink their own urine?”

verses.text: Restore us, O God of Hosts, and cause Your face to shine upon us, that we may be saved.

xrefs.text: Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a right spirit within me.
You welcome those who gladly do right, who remember Your ways. Surely You were angry, for we sinned. How can we be saved if we remain in our sins?
Restore us, O LORD God of Hosts; cause Your face to shine upon us, that we may be saved.
Wash the evil from your heart, O Jerusalem, so that you may be saved. How long will you harbor wicked thoughts within you?
Restore us, O God, and cause Your face to shine upon us, that we may be saved.

verses.text: You uprooted a vine from Egypt; You drove out the nations and transplanted it.

xrefs.text: I had planted you like a choice vine from the very best seed. How could you turn yourself before Me into a rotten, wild vine?
With Your hand You drove out the nations and planted our fathers there; You crushed the peoples and cast them out.
It sprouted and became a spreading vine, low in height, with branches turned toward him; yet its roots remained where it stood. So it became a vine and yielded branches and sent out shoots.
I will sing for my beloved a song of his vineyard: My beloved had a vineyard on a very fertile hill.
Many shepherds have destroyed My vineyard; they have trampled My plot of ground. They have turned My pleasant field into a desolate wasteland.

verses.text: You cleared the ground for it, and it took root and filled the land.

xrefs.text: I sent the hornet ahead of you, and it drove out the two Amorite kings before you, but not by your own sword or bow.
I will send the hornet before you to drive the Hivites and Canaanites and Hittites out of your way.
In the days to come, Jacob will take root. Israel will bud and blossom and fill the whole world with fruit.
You planted them, and they have taken root. They have grown and produced fruit. You are ever on their lips, but far from their hearts.
You gave them kingdoms and peoples and allotted to them every corner of the land. So they took the land of Sihon king of Heshbon and of Og king of Bashan.

verses.text: The mountains were covered by its shade, and the mighty cedars with its branches.

xrefs.text: The trees of the LORD have their fill, the cedars of Lebanon that He planted,

verses.text: It sent out its branches to the Sea, and its shoots toward the River.

xrefs.text: May he rule from sea to sea, and from the Euphrates to the ends of the earth.

And I will establish your borders from the Red Sea to the Sea of the Philistines, and from the desert to the Euphrates. For I will deliver the inhabitants into your hand, and you will drive them out before you.
On that day the LORD made a covenant with Abram, saying, “To your descendants I have given this land— from the river of Egypt to the great River Euphrates —
As far as Hamath, David also defeated King Hadadezer of Zobah, who had marched out to establish his dominion along the Euphrates River.
And Solomon reigned over all the kingdoms from the Euphrates to the land of the Philistines, as far as the border of Egypt. These kingdoms offered tribute and served Solomon all the days of his life.

verses.text: Why have You broken down its walls, so that all who pass by pick its fruit?

xrefs.text: Now I will tell you what I am about to do to My vineyard: I will take away its hedge, and it will be consumed; I will tear down its wall, and it will be trampled.
He will come and kill those tenants and give the vineyard to others. And when the people heard this, they said, “May such a thing never happen!
You have broken down all his walls; You have reduced his strongholds to rubble.
For before the harvest, when the blossom is gone and the flower becomes a ripening grape, He will cut off the shoots with a pruning knife and remove and discard the branches.
For the LORD will restore the splendor of Jacob like the splendor of Israel, though destroyers have laid them waste and ruined the branches of their vine.

verses.text: The boar from the forest ravages it, and the creatures of the field feed upon it.

xrefs.text: A lion has gone up from his thicket, and a destroyer of nations has set out. He has left his lair to lay waste your land. Your cities will be reduced to ruins and lie uninhabited.

Therefore a lion from the forest will strike them down, a wolf from the desert will ravage them. A leopard will lie in wait near their cities, and everyone who ventures out will be torn to pieces. For their rebellious acts are many, and their unfaithful deeds are numerous.

Then the city was breached; and though the Chaldeans had surrounded the city, all the men of war fled the city by night by way of the gate between the two walls near the king’s garden. They headed toward the Arabah,
Then the people of the land took Jehoahaz son of Josiah and made him king in Jerusalem in place of his father.
After all these acts of faithfulness, Sennacherib king of Assyria came and invaded Judah. He laid siege to the fortified cities, intending to conquer them for himself.

verses.text: Return, O God of Hosts, we pray! Look down from heaven and see! Attend to this vine—

xrefs.text: Look down from heaven and see, from Your holy and glorious habitation. Where are Your zeal and might? Your yearning and compassion for me are restrained.
Why, O LORD, do You make us stray from Your ways and harden our hearts from fearing You? Return, for the sake of Your servants, the tribes of Your heritage.
Return, O LORD! How long will it be? Have compassion on Your servants.
Yet from the days of your fathers, you have turned away from My statutes and have not kept them. Return to Me, and I will return to you,” says the LORD of Hosts. “But you ask, ‘How can we return?’

O Lord, in keeping with all Your righteous acts, I pray that Your anger and wrath may turn away from Your city Jerusalem, Your holy mountain; for because of our sins and the iniquities of our fathers, Jerusalem and Your people are a reproach to all around us.

verses.text: the root Your right hand has planted, the son You have raised up for Yourself.

xrefs.text: [“]I am the true vine, and My Father is the keeper of the vineyard.
And you are to tell him that this is what the LORD of Hosts says: ‘Here is a man whose name is the Branch, and He will branch out from His place and build the temple of the LORD.
Hear now, O high priest Joshua, you and your companions seated before you, who are indeed a sign. For behold, I am going to bring My servant, the Branch.

Then Jesus began to speak to them in parables: “A man planted a vineyard. He put a wall around it, dug a wine vat, and built a watchtower. Then he rented it out to some tenants and went away on a journey.
Behold, the days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will raise up for David a righteous Branch, and He will reign wisely as King and will administer justice and righteousness in the land.

verses.text: Your vine has been cut down and burned; they perish at the rebuke of Your countenance.

xrefs.text: You discipline and correct a man for his iniquity, consuming like a moth what he holds dear; surely each man is but a vapor. Selah
If anyone does not remain in Me, he is like a branch that is thrown away and withers. Such branches are gathered up, thrown into the fire, and burned.
They will suffer the penalty of eternal destruction, separated from the presence of the Lord and the glory of His might,
For we are consumed by Your anger and terrified by Your wrath.

When its limbs are dry, they are broken off. Women come and use them for kindling; for this is a people without understanding. Therefore their Maker has no compassion on them, and their Creator shows them no favor.

verses.text: Let Your hand be upon the man at Your right hand, on the son of man You have raised up for Yourself.

xrefs.text: In my vision in the night I continued to watch, and I saw One like the Son of Man coming with the clouds of heaven. He approached the Ancient of Days and was led into His presence.
A Psalm of David. The LORD said to my Lord: “Sit at My right hand until I make Your enemies a footstool for Your feet.”
My hand will sustain him; surely My arm will strengthen him.
the root Your right hand has planted, the son You have raised up for Yourself.
For just as the Father raises the dead and gives them life, so also the Son gives life to whom He wishes.

verses.text: Then we will not turn away from You; revive us, and we will call on Your name.

xrefs.text: How I long for Your precepts! Revive me in Your righteousness.
Therefore, my beloved, just as you have always obeyed, not only in my presence, but now even more in my absence, continue to work out your salvation with fear and trembling.
My soul cleaves to the dust; revive me according to Your word.
Defend my cause and redeem me; revive me according to Your word.
I am severely afflicted, O LORD; revive me through Your word.

verses.text: Restore us, O LORD God of Hosts; cause Your face to shine upon us, that we may be saved.

xrefs.text: “Return, O faithless children, and I will heal your faithlessness.” “Here we are. We come to You, for You are the LORD our God.
One thing I have asked of the LORD; this is what I desire: to dwell in the house of the LORD all the days of my life, to gaze on the beauty of the LORD and seek Him in His temple.
Restore us, O God, and cause Your face to shine upon us, that we may be saved.
For it was not by their sword that they took the land; their arm did not bring them victory. It was by Your right hand, Your arm, and the light of Your face, because You favored them.
